records.summary: On 4 October 2016 the Ministry of Finance of the Republic of Croatia asked the European Central Bank for an opinion on a draft act amending the Act on the Croatian National Bank (Hrvatska Narodna Banka, HNB). The ECB replied on 28 October 2016 in Opinion CON/2016/52. The draft would let the State Audit Office carry out an annual audit of HNB's business operations, including an efficiency review, with HNB obliged to hand over documents and give access to classified material, and it would require HNB to send semi-annual information and an annual report to the Croatian Parliament, which would vote on whether to adopt them. The ECB said central bank powers must not be subject to external instructions or government influence, that state audits should be non-political, independent and purely professional, and that in several respects the draft law is unclear, contradictory and fails to satisfy these requirements and safeguards. It said the State Audit Office should not verify or express opinions on HNB's financial statements, and that the written response HNB would owe on measures taken should not amount to a requirement of HNB to receive instructions from the State Auditor. On the parliamentary vote, the ECB said Parliament's competence to vote on these reports would affect HNB's institutional independence, and that any parliamentary right to approve, suspend, annul or defer HNB's decisions would conflict with that independence. The draft also capped Council members at two six-year terms, with transitional protection for sitting members, and barred the State Audit Office from proposing the dismissal of any Council member.
records.source_title: Opinion of the European Central Bank of 28 October 2016 on a draft act on amendments to the Act on the Croatian National Bank (CON/2016/52) (European Central Bank, 28 October 2016)

records.summary: On 5 March 2015 Bulgaria's Parliament voted 84 to 0 to set up an ad hoc committee of inquiry into the collapse of Corporate Commercial Bank (CCB, also called Corpbank). The committee was to examine the conduct of the state bodies and institutions meant by law to exercise control that should have prevented the draining of the bank, covering the years 2009 to 2014. Among the bodies whose actions it was to examine was the banking supervision arm of the Bulgarian National Bank (BNB), alongside the Financial Supervision Commission and the financial intelligence department of the State Agency for National Security. The memorandum setting up the committee said the BNB's banking supervision should closely monitor compliance with good financial practices. Bulgarian news agency BTA separately reported that the ad hoc committee of inquiry into the Corpbank failure gave a hearing to the central bank governor on 24 March 2015. The Sofia Globe report does not name governor Ivan Iskrov.
records.source_title: Bulgarian Parliament sets up committee of inquiry into Corporate Commercial Bank affair (The Sofia Globe, 5 March 2015)

records.summary: In December 2014 the European Central Bank warned that proposed amendments to Bulgaria's Deposit Insurance Act could infringe the independence of the Bulgarian National Bank (BNB). The BNB made the warning public, citing a letter from ECB President Mario Draghi. The letter, as reported, said the draft would prevent the BNB from investing and managing its reserves and would require provisional transfers to the Deposit Insurance Fund. The ECB argued that if the BNB were allowed to make such transfers, the central bank's own resources and reserve could be severely limited, which would hinder its work within the European System of Central Banks, and that the draft could jeopardise the stability of Bulgaria's currency board. The report does not say which body tabled the amendments; it notes the Bulgarian government was considering direct grants to the Deposit Insurance Fund instead. Bulgarian news agency BTA later carried the headline 'ECB: Bank Deposit Guarantee Act Impairs BNB's Institutional and Financial Independence', but that page is behind a sign-in wall and was not read.
records.source_title: ECB: Proposed Changes to Bulgaria Deposit Insurance Law Harm C-Bank (Novinite / Sofia News Agency, 10 December 2014)

records.summary: In October 2022 Dejan Djurovic, a member of the Montenegrin Parliament for the Democratic Front, tabled amendments to the Central Bank of Montenegro Law. The amendments would remove the President of Montenegro from the process of proposing the governor, so that Parliament would elect the governor on the proposal of the parliamentary Committee on Economy, Finance and Budget, which Djurovic himself chairs. They would also end the six-year mandates of vice-governor Zorica Kalezic and three members of the Central Bank Council, with replacements to be appointed within 90 days, and would raise the work experience required of the governor and vice-governors from five to ten years. The move followed President Milo Djukanovic's proposal in September 2022 of a further six-year term for governor Radoje Zugic. The Central Bank of Montenegro said the proposal does not democratise the selection process and directly undermines ('direktno potkopava') the bank's guaranteed independence, that cutting short the Council's mandates could put the closing of EU accession Chapter 17 at risk and call into question Montenegro's use of the euro after accession, and that it would subordinate the bank to electoral cycles and political interests. IMF mission chief Srikant Seshadri told Radio Free Europe that the Fund had told Parliament directly that the existing system should not change, describing the 'double veto' as consistent with international best practice. The article, dated 12 April 2023, reported the proposal was on the parliamentary agenda and expected to pass.
records.source_title: Radio Free Europe / Radio Liberty report on the Central Bank of Montenegro and the Democratic Front's draft amendments (Radio Slobodna Evropa, 12 April 2023)

records.summary: At the end of September 2017 five members of Estonia's Riigikogu, from the EKRE, Vabaerakond and Keskerakond groups, initiated a bill to compensate holders of VEB Fund certificates for their losses out of Eesti Pank's profit distributions. Under the proposal Parliament would make a preliminary decision directing 50 per cent of the central bank's annual profit distribution to the state budget to the certificate holders until the compensation was paid in full. The total was put at 10 to 15 million euros including interest, with up to about 15 million euros expected to come from Eesti Pank's profit distributions; Keskerakond deputy chairman Jaanus Karilaid, a leading proponent, suggested payments could run from 2019 to 2023. Eesti Pank responded that its council decides on the distribution of its profit and is independent in that decision, and that the proposers want to use money already paid into the state budget, or to be paid in future, as profit distributions. The report is dated 15 January 2018 and says the bill still needed parliamentary support.
records.source_title: Eelnou seob VEB fondi kahjude huvitamise Eesti Panga kasumiga (ERR, 15 January 2018)

records.summary: This is a standing arrangement, not a dated episode, and it has no end date. Kuwait's central bank law, Law No. 32 of 1968, as published in English by the Central Bank of Kuwait itself, lets the executive direct the bank. Article 38 provides that the Minister of Finance may issue directives to the bank and that such directives shall become binding on the Bank; if the Board of Directors objects, the Minister refers the matter to the Council of Ministers, and the decision of the Council of Ministers on the matter shall be final. Article 27 lets the Ministry of Finance's representative on the Board request that a monetary policy resolution be suspended, which is then referred to the Minister, with the resolution taking effect only if the Minister does not decide within seven days. Article 24 requires the Minister of Finance's representative or alternate to be present for a quorum, and Article 23 requires the Governor to convene the Board if the Minister of Finance asks. The Governor and Deputy Governor are appointed by decree on the recommendation of the Minister of Finance (Article 19), their pay is set by the Council of Ministers, and under Article 22(2) a Board member's service, the Governor's included, may be terminated by decree by a decision of the Council of Ministers for a grave violation of duties or for missing all Board meetings for three consecutive months without approval. Board approval of the budget estimates and the balance sheet must be sanctioned by the Minister of Finance (Article 26(13)).
records.source_title: Law No. 32 of 1968 concerning Currency, the Central Bank of Kuwait and the Organisation of Banking Business, Chapter II: Central Bank of Kuwait (Central Bank of Kuwait, English text)

records.summary: This is a standing arrangement, not a dated episode, and it has no end date. On the State Bank of Vietnam's own English-language page setting out the 2010 Law on the State Bank of Vietnam, the bank states that the National Assembly determines the annual inflation target and oversees how national monetary policy is carried out, and that the Government submits the annual inflation target to the National Assembly for determination. The Prime Minister and the SBV Governor determine the use of monetary policy tools and measures, and those choices must serve the policy objectives the Government sets. On this statement of its own governing law the bank does not set its own policy target: the target is fixed by the legislature on the Government's proposal, and the Prime Minister stands alongside the Governor in choosing the instruments.
records.source_title: Monetary policy decision-making authority and monetary policy tools (State Bank of Vietnam, English site)

records.summary: This is a standing arrangement, not a dated episode, and it has no end date. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority describes in its own annual report how it was set up: the Legislative Council passed amendments to the Exchange Fund Ordinance in 1992 empowering the Financial Secretary to appoint a Monetary Authority, and the HKMA began work on 1 April 1993. The Monetary Authority is appointed under the Exchange Fund Ordinance to assist the Financial Secretary, and the Exchange Fund, which backs the currency, is established by that Ordinance under the control of the Financial Secretary. The division of functions between the Financial Secretary and the Monetary Authority is set out in an exchange of letters dated 25 June 2003 which discloses delegations made by the Financial Secretary to the Monetary Authority, and the Monetary Authority also performs functions assigned by other Ordinances or by the Financial Secretary. On the HKMA's own account, then, the person who heads Hong Kong's central banking institution is appointed by a government minister and exercises powers that minister delegates.
records.source_title: About the HKMA, HKMA Annual Report 2025 (Hong Kong Monetary Authority)

FILED. The part of that draft that changes who proposes the governor is an appointment matter and is not the reason for filing; the early termination of sitting mandates is.
